title: Learn, Inform and Quiet
summary: Choose how much Kneady tells you: Learn's tutorials and complete tips, Inform's shorter tips, or Quiet.

steps.title: Step 1: Learn Shows Everything
text: 1. Rest the mouse on the button on the cube's top. After half a second, its tip shows under its name, listing every key: each drag, Ctrl, Shift, Shift+Click.
That's Learn, where Kneady starts: complete tips, and the tutorials offered at the top of the Kneady tab. The cube's control is one you'll make in Quick Start.

media.label: On the cube, then in the Kneady tab

steps.title: Step 2: Inform Says Less
text: 1. In the Kneady tab, Help says Learn. Set it to Inform.
2. Rest the mouse on the cube's button: its tip shows only what each drag does. Start a Tutorial is gone from the top of the tab.

Inform is for when you know your way around: the keys every button shares are left to the status bar, at the foot of the window. The tab offers no tutorials - this one keeps playing - but a file that comes with its own still shows them, as Tutorials in This File.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the cube

steps.title: Step 3: Quiet Says Least
text: 2. Rest the mouse on the cube's button: its name shows, and no tip.
Quiet keeps out of the way: the buttons' names and the status bar, nothing more. Every button works just as before.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the cube

steps.title: Step 4: Back to Learn
text: 1. Set Help back to Learn: Start a Tutorial is back.

Help is yours, not the file's: it stays as you leave it in every file you open, until you change it. Keep Learn for the tutorials - next is 1. Quick Start - and choose Inform or Quiet when you're done with them.
